content.title: About
content.content: Egg bread roll is a soft, slightly sweet bread roll made from eggs, milk, butter and wheat flour. The dough rises, is shaped into a long roll and baked until golden. It is commonly used as a base for sandwiches, snacks and breakfasts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg bread originated in Europe in the 19th century as a more nourishing bread variant.
Traditionally the roll is sliced thin and served with butter or cheese.
In some countries the egg bread roll is called "brioche" – although the recipes differ, both are enriched with eggs and butter.
The dough is often enriched with milk and butter, giving it a tender, aromatic crumb.
The roll stores well in the refrigerator for up to a week without loss of flavor.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and milk provide a high-quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The dough contains B12, riboflavin and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Dairy ingredients supply calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates from wheat flour give a quick source of energy, making the roll a good breakfast option.

items.title: Vitamin D content
items.content: When fortified milk is used, the product can provide vitamin D, which aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Egg and milk allergy
items.content: People allergic to eggs or dairy should avoid this product as it may trigger reactions.

items.title: High sugar and fat content
items.content: Some recipes add sugar and a generous amount of butter, increasing caloric density.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat flour contains gluten, making the roll unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt can be a concern for individuals monitoring sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Egg bread roll can be eaten fresh, toasted, with butter, cheese, ham or vegetables. It is often used as a base for sandwiches and snacks. Cut into cubes for salads or soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the roll in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage keep it refrigerated – up to 5–7 days. Freeze in a freezer‑safe bag if you need to keep it for more than a month; thaw at room temperature before use.
